transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-30
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes (call hung up at 17:02)
Attendees: Alex Greene (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (Halcyon VP Eng), Sofia Martinez (Halcyon Head Security), Evan Brooks (Halcyon Procurement)

Summary:
Quick kickoff to finalize MSA/DPA redlines around privileged access and KMS, align on migration plan from their incumbent provider, and surface procurement timelines for pricing approval. Main blockers: DPA keying language, SOC 2 artifact timing, and committed reserved capacity pricing.

Topics covered:
- DPA redlines: privileged keys, access logs, egress
- KMS/HSM options and customer-managed keys
- SLA targets and rollback policy for migration windows
- Pricing cadence: reserved capacity vs burst pricing
- Procurement timeline and approvers

Transcript:
00:00 Alex Greene: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, um this is alex from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, i'm gonna do a quick round robin, um maya from our solutions team is here to go into the tech bits, over to you halcyon can we do quick intros
00:12 Raj Patel: yeah sure i'm raj vp engineering, sofia head of security, and evan from procurement, uh thanks for making time
00:20 Maya Chen: hey all, maya chen, infra se, i'll handle the KMS and migration questions, sorry if my connection's a little crunchy at first
00:30 Alex Greene: cool, high level goal for today's call is to get alignment on DPA/msa redlines for privileged access and to map out next steps for migration / pricing approval, so we can start a pilot next month
00:45 Raj Patel: sounds good, our exec wants to make sure that any privileged keys used by the model inference path are customer-controlled, and that audit logs are available for 18 months, that's the initial ask
00:56 Sofia Martinez: yes, and from security, we need SOC 2 artifacts and evidence of key rotation and HSM usage or equivalent, plus a clear RBAC model for who at Redwood could see raw customer prompts. we can't have broad access in the clear
01:15 Maya Chen: right, so quick framing: Redwood supports three deployment modes, hosted, dedicated, and private/vpc. for the dedicated and private options we can offer CMK (customer-managed keys) integrated with your cloud ksm — we call it KMS tie-in, but sorry sometimes the doc calls it devoted k... redwood devoted, that's a typo in the doc
01:35 Raj Patel: heh, yes we saw that, the legal team kept reading 'redwood devoted' in the draft, so that was funny. but more importantly, for our use-case, can you explain the difference between dedicated with CMK vs private on-prem with HSM? latency and data flow concerns are huge for payments
01:50 Maya Chen: sure. dedicated is still Redwood-managed infra but isolated pool with tenant isolation and CMK integration for encrypting model checkpoints and logs at rest; private is full customer-managed control plane where you bring networking and optionally HSMs — private gives you the strongest isolation but requires your ops to handle upgrades and some of the rollout orchestration. latency is typically comparable if the private cluster lives in same region, but on-prem will add network variability if it's on-premise behind their firewall
02:15 Sofia Martinez: and what about audit logs? we need immutable audit trails, and retention controls — the DPA currently has a 90-day retention clause which is not enough for us
02:27 Alex Greene: understood. on the DPA redline we can extend retention to 18 months for log records tied to privileged access, and we can supply syslog exports for ingestion into your SIEM. that was one of the proposed edits i flagged in the draft
02:40 Evan Brooks: procurement question — what's the billing shape for reserved capacity? i need an estimate to present to finance. are there quarterly commitments or annual? and what's the penalty if we scale down after three months?
02:56 Maya Chen: reserved capacity is typically monthly or annual commits; our pricing worksheet has both. for committed pools you get a discount on per-token and per-inference compute. if you scale down mid-term we can do a step-down on renewal, but the initial commit period depends on whether you want dedicated pools or private — private tends to be annual because of the capacity planning
03:20 Raj Patel: on the technical side — can Redwood's KV cache be flushed per-tenant? we need to ensure that any prompt context used during inference is not accessible after a session is terminated, right
03:33 Maya Chen: yes, per-tenant cache eviction is supported. there's an automatic TTL and a manual purge API; we'll include the API endpoints in the runbook. small caveat — during live migration we may need a transitional period where caches are warmed in the new pool to prevent latency spikes, but the KV contents are never shared between tenants
03:55 Sofia Martinez: okay good. back to the KMS clause, the DPA redline currently prevents us from using Redwood-managed keys for privileged inference. we need a commitment that raw prompts are only stored encrypted with our CMK and that Redwood personnel cannot decrypt them without a legal process (court order / subpoena)
04:20 Alex Greene: we can agree to CMKs and a policy that requires a two-person process to access decrypted data and that access is logged. however, I need to flag that for hosted API (the self-serve offering) CMKs for every account isn't supported today — it's a dedicated/private feature. we'll call that out in the amendment
04:45 Raj Patel: understood, our preference is dedicated or private — we want the isolation but not the full burden of on-prem just yet. what about SLA? we need a 99.9 uptime SLA for inference endpoints during business hours and a rollback plan if there's outage during migration windows
05:05 Maya Chen: SLA language: 99.9% is achievable with our dedicated pools; we have standard credits and a canary rollback policy. during migration we can configure traffic steering with gradual cutover and automatic fallback to the previous model/route if latency or error rates exceed thresholds — we'll document rollback runbook steps in the migration playbook
05:30 Sofia Martinez: will that be in the SLA or in the runbook? legal likes to see explicit rollback commitments in the MSA Appendix B
05:40 Alex Greene: good point — we can add a migration appendix that describes the rollback policy and the latency/error thresholds that trigger an automated fallback. that's doable
05:50 Evan Brooks: pricing again, two follow-ups: 1) can you provide a 90-day pilot price with committed reserved capacity for testing, and 2) what's the conversion credit if we convert pilot usage to enterprise commit?
06:03 Maya Chen: yes to both. we usually offer a pilot discount for the first 90 days and then a conversion credit that applies to the enterprise reserved commitment if you sign within 60 days of pilot end. i'll put numbers in the pricing worksheet i upload
06:17 Raj Patel: legal asked about third-party subprocessors. the DPA lists a few libs and infra partners, but we need a clause that any change to subprocessors triggers a 30-day notification and the right to object for regulatory reasons
06:33 Alex Greene: we can amend the DPA to add a 30-day notification clause for subprocessors and a carve-out process for regulatory objections. that will be in the redline i circulate
06:45 Sofia Martinez: also, we require evidence of ISO 27001 or equivalent for any partner who might touch customer data. do you have that?
06:54 Maya Chen: Redwood's infrastructure partners maintain SOC 2 Type II, and we're in the process of finalizing ISO artifacts — timeline is Q3 for ISO but we can provide the SOC 2 report and a letter of attestation in the meantime. i'll include that in the doc share
07:10 Raj Patel: on encryption in transit, for private deployments can we force mutual TLS between our client gateways and the Redwood inference nodes? we have strict mTLS requirements for payments flows
07:22 Maya Chen: yes mTLS is supported for private deployments and we can configure certs issued by your CA. for dedicated we can do TLS with client cert pinning, and the runbook will detail cert rotation schedules
07:36 Evan Brooks: procurement will want the indemnity and data residency pieces cleared before showstopping the deal — any surprises there?
07:46 Alex Greene: standard indemnity clauses apply; we can follow the company's enterprise playbook. on data residency, dedicated pools can be pinned to region, and we can do data residency commitments in the MSA. anything specific you need?
07:58 Sofia Martinez: we need to lock EU data to EU regionally for European cards, and US data in US. we also need to confirm backup retention and cross-region replication controls
08:12 Maya Chen: we can set the region affinity per-customer; backup replication is configurable and we'll ensure backups for EU-resident datasets stay within EU, no cross-region replication unless explicitly enabled by you
08:27 Raj Patel: ok good. quick question about access: you mentioned a two-person process for decrypting data — is that automated through KMS policies or is there a human approval step? legal prefers automated workflows where possible
08:40 Alex Greene: the ideal flow is automated gating through KMS policies and IAM, with human review logged as an exception path. so automated by default, exception requires two-person approval and will generate audit tickets
08:56 Sofia Martinez: great. regarding the DPA redline, we have a couple of edits around breach notification windows — we need a 48-hour window for initial notice and 30 days for full report, is that acceptable?
09:09 Alex Greene: 48/30 is reasonable; we'll propose that in the redline and note it as negotiable for high-sensitivity incidents where additional measures may apply
09:20 Raj Patel: migration specifics — if we switch from our current vendor, can Redwood ingest model weights and then match latency profiles? our SRE is worried about tokenization mismatches and cold-start penalties
09:33 Maya Chen: marshaling model weights: if it's an open model we can import weights directly; for tokenization we will run a verification suite to ensure inference parity and provide burn-in windows. cold-starts can be addressed by pre-warming caches and pre-populating KV with commonly used prefixes — all part of the migration playbook
09:55 Evan Brooks: any risk of data being in-flight during migration that could violate our compliance?
10:03 Alex Greene: migration happens over encrypted channels, and we can opt for an in-region staging cluster so data never leaves designated jurisdictions. we'll include acceptance criteria for data-in-transit encryption and ephemeral storage controls
10:20 Sofia Martinez: okay, back to procurement process: Evan will need a vendor package with SOC 2, insurance certificates, sample MSA redline and estimated SOW costs. Evan?
10:32 Evan Brooks: yes i'll need that to present to finance & legal. timeline wise i need the MSA and pricing no later than 2026-05-06 to hit our committee next week
10:40 Alex Greene: we'll aim for 2026-05-04 for the redline and 05-06 for the full pricing + runbook bundle — aligns with our internal to-dos
10:52 Raj Patel: any blockers from Redwood side that would prevent us from meeting those dates?
10:58 Maya Chen: none immediate; SE team is ready to generate the runbook and pricing sheet. we might need a short security interview for the SOC artifacts but that's a doc request not a blocker
11:10 Sofia Martinez: one last security ask — can you provide a sample key rotation schedule and proof that rotation can be done without downtime?
11:20 Maya Chen: yes, there is a zero-downtime rotation procedure for CMKs using dual-keying and re-encryption handoff. i'll include the tech note and a diagram in the runbook
11:33 Raj Patel: great. ok i think that's the meat of it. as a recap can we list the top three deliverables and owners?
11:40 Alex Greene: sure, i'll recap: 1) Redline MSA/DPA with KMS and subprocessor clauses — owner: Alex — due 2026-05-04. 2) Dedicated pricing worksheet + 90-day pilot offer and migration runbook — owner: Maya — due 2026-05-06. 3) Halcyon to provide privileged roles list and procurement approver timeline — owner: Raj/Evan — due 2026-05-08
11:58 Evan Brooks: yep i'll aim to get approvers list by 05-05, maybe 05-06 latest
12:05 Sofia Martinez: i'll follow up if we need a separate technical deep dive on HSMs
12:12 Alex Greene: perfect, thanks everyone. we'll send the redline and pricing and schedule a follow-up for next Tuesday if that works for Halcyon
12:22 Raj Patel: next tuesday works for me, thanks all
12:30 (call ends at 17:02 UTC)

Notes about transcript: occasional crosstalk and micro-pauses, some words auto-transcribed incorrectly (e.g., 'Redwood Devoted' instead of 'Redwood Dedicated'), timestamps are approximate, and some proper nouns may be slightly off. Links referenced: Pricing worksheet (link shared in chat), Draft MSA redline (will be shared by Alex), Migration runbook template (to be uploaded by Maya).
